hero.thesis: Easier to understand. Easier to use.
intro: Finding what you need, making a choice, applying for a service. Everyday actions that often hide complex processes. My work is to understand those processes and the people who face them, so that the digital solutions we build are well thought through.
More than ten years in design: from Tet TV+ to insurance and public digital services. Both designing myself and leading teams.

items.title: An unclear problem
items.situation: Everyone feels something is not working, but no one can say what exactly.
items.action: Users and customer-service staff are researched, data is analysed, and the problem is defined together with the team in a workshop.
items.outcome: Decisions rest on evidence rather than guesses, before development money is spent.

items.title: A complex service
items.situation: The service is correct in substance, but people do not understand it or do not complete it.
items.action: The journey from customer to employee is mapped, prototypes are built and tested with users, and the finished solution is handed over to development.
items.outcome: A service people can complete on their own, and fewer calls to support.

items.title: Stakeholders cannot agree
items.situation: Business, IT and marketing each see a different goal, and decisions get stuck.
items.action: In workshops and design critique, opinions are turned into shared goals and measurable indicators.
items.outcome: One direction, and decisions that do not come back at the next meeting.

items.title: Design without a system
items.situation: There is design, but every product looks and works differently.
items.action: A design system, process and team are built; accessibility becomes an everyday standard rather than a final check.
items.outcome: A consistent product across platforms and cheaper development.

work.heading: A few projects that mattered
work.lead: Each one starts with a problem: a business challenge or a user need that has not been met.

items.title: Baltic Claims system and partner portal
items.text: A claims-handling system used daily by claims specialists across the Baltics. User interviews were carried out to uncover the main pain points, and the findings were turned into concrete UX and UI improvements: simpler flows and a clearer visual hierarchy. The partner portal was substantially improved as well. The work was done in close collaboration with developers and business analysts.
items.imageAlt: Baltic Claims system screen: claim details, notes and tasks

items.role: UX/UI Designer, later Head of UX & Service Design
items.title: Fully digital personal accident insurance purchase
items.text: A new, fully digital personal accident insurance webshop, designed from scratch through the full UX/UI cycle. The user journey was defined, prototypes were built and tested with users, and a clear, purchase-focused experience was handed over to development. The solution covers both customers and front-line staff, including internal tooling for customer support.
items.imageAlt: Personal accident insurance purchase, coverage step with price summary

items.org: Latvijas Banka, a Zen IS project
items.title: Mana pensija
items.text: A site that explains the Latvian pension system and helps people choose a plan. The work was led from secondary data and competitor analysis through user research, personas, concept and prototype tests (36 interviews and tests in total), as well as problem-definition workshops with the client. Dense financial information became clear pages with calculators, comparisons and a design system.
items.imageAlt: manapensija.lv home page with age-group sections

items.title: business.gov.lv, state services for entrepreneurs
items.text: A portal that brings state e-services for entrepreneurs into one place and guides them through complex processes. Goals, target groups and KPIs were set in a workshop with LIAA stakeholders; new layouts for public and authorised users were designed and user-tested; and a scalable design system was built with clear foundations for colour, typography and components.
items.imageAlt: business.gov.lv home page with service search and main sections

items.title: Design-thinking programme for app development
items.text: A twelve-week design-thinking programme aimed at making the app Tele2's main digital point of contact with customers. The programme was created and run end to end: 20 participants in four teams, each with its own user focus, four on-site workshops and five online sessions. Together with a UI designer, the teams' ideas were developed into an app design solution on a shared design system.
items.imageAlt: Three Tele2 app screens: invoice, offer and TV package selection

items.title: Tet.lv redesign and design system
items.text: The Tet.lv website redesign after the rebrand, leading the UI team: concept with the team, UI roadmap, workshops and communication with stakeholders and marketing. Alongside, a design system was built from scratch: guidelines and components rolled out step by step across products and reused in Storybook to reduce development costs.
items.imageAlt: Tet.lv redesign on laptop and phone: themed TV packages

about.heading: About
bio: I am Elīna Ozola, a UX and service designer from Latvia; until now I have also been known professionally as Elīna Ozola-Tērauda. I have worked in design for more than ten years: I started in graphic and web design, moved into product design across platforms (web, iOS, Android and TV) and in recent years focused on user research, service design and building design teams.

I currently work in user research and design at BTA, building the UX practice and design-system foundations, running user research and designing digital solutions. Before that I led the Research & Design team at Zen IS and UX and service design at If P&C Insurance in the Baltics. I run design-thinking workshops and programmes and teach accessibility and user-centred content to public-sector teams. In 2026 I completed a degree in business management at Turība University.

approach.heading: Different industries. Focus on people.
paragraphs: Television, insurance, a public service. Different industries, but on the other side there is always a person with their own goal, questions and obstacles. The work starts with understanding those people and ends with a solution that works.

Tet, If, Zen IS and BTA projects have produced customer apps and websites as well as the systems employees use every day. Alongside product work: leading design teams, running design-thinking workshops and teaching user-centred content and accessibility.
